notes: Close of the local-first web prototype: a Next.js PWA with everything held in the browser. Pebbles at this point has its path timeline, the quick pebble editor, collections, souls, glyphs and the carve canvas, onboarding, local accounts, the pigment colour worlds, the pebble artwork, offline install, karma and the bounce streak, and the bilingual legal docs. The next day the repository becomes a monorepo and the browser storage is replaced by a real backend.

The iPhone app went from an empty shell to near parity with the web app: signup, path, recording, editing and deleting pebbles, souls, collections, glyph carving, onboarding, the welcome screen, photos, the pebble reading page, French, and the Lab tab. No git tag or marketing version exists in the corpus for this period, so the era slug is used as the version.

notes: The back-office and the analytics suite. Pebbles gets a place to look at itself: an Analytics page built card by card, from headline numbers and active people to retention, volume and richness, per-person averages, the spread of emotions and life domains, how steady everyone's rhythm is, quality signals that admit what they cannot yet measure, and how many marks people carve themselves. Alongside it, the iPhone app learns to sign you in with Apple or Google, opens on a logo that draws itself, redraws its login and signup screens, lets a moment hold several people, and starts colouring pebbles with the palette of the feeling behind them, on the web as well.

description: An experiment, never shipped to anyone on a public build. PRs #556 (iOS), #557 (web) and #558 (Android) port one SVG feTurbulence displacement pipeline to all three surfaces so strokes look hand-carved rather than machine-drawn, gated on a golden-parity test; #559 then bakes it into Android's Play internal-testing bundles only. It is compiled out of production everywhere: iOS gates it behind #if DEBUG, web behind a dev-only flag stripped from production builds, and Android behind BuildConfig.WOBBLE_ENABLED, which defaults to false outside the android-release workflow. Recorded as a proposal, not a deliverable, precisely because no user has ever seen it.

In eight days a third client went from an empty Gradle module to Lab parity with iOS: the entry funnel, the read-only Path, recording and editing pebbles, path stats, profile and settings, souls, collections, snaps, the Glyph Studio and store, and the Lab. The Android arc itself completed at the M44 exit (#597, 2026-07-17T08:35:59Z); the rest of the era is cross-surface polish, so the tag sits at the era's last merge. notes: Close of the "Getting store-ready" era. Pebbles picks up everything the app stores needed and a lot people will actually feel: closing your account for good from Settings on all three surfaces, half-formed pebbles you can save and come back to with the composer remembering what you were typing, achievements with a shelf on your profile and a little moment when one unlocks, a handle and an optional public page you can share, and connections you invite by link or QR code. Underneath, the promise that your path is only yours was quietly repaired. The corpus carries GitHub milestones M46 to M50 for this period but no git tag, no marketing version and no single milestone covering the era, so the era slug is used as the version, matching the other eras in this run.
